question: In recent days there have been a growing number of official reports of new incidents of religious violence in the Christian town of Al-Suqaylabiyah in Syria. Sunni armed groups attacked residents, harassed women, caused material damage and vandalised places of worship1.

The authorities arrested members of the local Christian community who attempted to protect their families and property, leaving the main perpetrators unpunished2. The Greek Orthodox Patriarchate of Antioch and other Christian Churches have called for a full and impartial investigation3.

These incidents raise serious concerns about the state of human rights, religious freedom and protection of indigenous Christian communities in Syria, which are an integral part of the region’s historic and cultural heritage.

In view of the above, can the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy answer the following: Does she consider that the necessary conditions for the protection of human rights are being met by the Syrian authorities?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (4.11.2026) Since the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024, the EU has closely followed developments in Syria and has consistently underlined that the transition can only succeed if it is genuinely inclusive and protects the rights of Syrians from all ethnic and religious background without any kind of discrimination.

This was also a message that the High Representative/Vice President conveyed to all interlocutors during the visit to Syria on 29 September 2026. The EU recognises the important role of Syria’s diverse communities, including its Christian population, in shaping an inclusive future for the country.
With regard to the incidents referred to, the EU condemns all violence and intimidation targeting communities on any grounds including religious ones, as well as any related human rights violations.

Within its discussions with Syria’s transitional authorities, the EU reiterates that this is instrumental for pursuing national reconciliation and an inclusive transition and stresses the responsibility of the Syrian transitional authorities to ensure the safety and fundamental rights of all Syrians.

The EU has consistently called for a full and impartial investigation into such incidents and for accountability for all perpetrators. These elements are essential for building trust, advancing national reconciliation and ensuring respect for the rule of law.

The EU continues to engage with the Syrian transitional authorities on the need to uphold human rights and fundamental freedoms, and to ensure the protection of all Syrians. These are essential conditions for achieving a peaceful and genuinely inclusive transition.

The EU remains vigilant about the respect for human rights of all Syrians and will continue to support comprehensive accountability efforts for all perpetrators regardless of their affiliation. In May1 and June2 2025, the EU introduced new listings against human rights violators and will continue monitoring the situation on the ground and the follow up of the commitments of the transitional authorities.
1 Council Decision (CFSP) 2025/1110 of 28 May 2025 amending Decision (CFSP) 2020/1999 concerning

restrictive measures against serious human rights violations and abuses, OJ L, 2025/1110, 28.5.2025, ELI: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=OJ:L_202501110. 2 Council Decision (CFSP) 2025/1255 of 23 June 2025 amending Decision (CFSP) 2020/1999 concerning restrictive measures against serious human rights violations and abuses, OJ L, 2025/1255, 23.6.2025, ELI: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=OJ:L_202501255.
